title: 9-DOF IMU Chip Layout
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Interactive Mermaid diagram of the swarm robot's 9-DOF IMU module: an L3GD20 gyroscope at I2C address 0x6B and an LSM303DLHC accelerometer (0x19) and magnetometer (0x1E), plus an unused BMP180 (0x77), sharing I2C bus 0 on Pico W GPIO16/17. Scenario buttons show the i2c.scan() output when every chip answers or when one chip's wiring fails.

educational.topic: 9-DOF IMU chips on a shared I2C bus
learningObjectives: Explain that a 9-DOF IMU module is two separate I2C chips sharing one bus.
Identify the I2C addresses of the L3GD20 gyroscope (0x6B) and the LSM303DLHC accelerometer (0x19) and magnetometer (0x1E).
Match each chip to the data it provides and its units (deg/s, g, gauss).
Interpret an i2c.scan() result that lists only one address.
prerequisites: I2C buses, SDA/SCL, and device addresses (Chapter 6)
Reading an I2C sensor with readfrom_mem() (Chapter 8)
standards: CSTA 3A-CS-02: Compare levels of abstraction and interactions between application software, system software, and hardware layers.

controls.label: All chips answer
controls.purpose: Normal module: the scan lists 0x19, 0x1e, 0x6b, and 0x77 (default).

controls.label: Gyro not answering
controls.purpose: The L3GD20 wiring has failed: 0x6b is missing from the scan.

controls.label: Accel/Mag not answering
controls.purpose: The LSM303DLHC wiring has failed: 0x19 and 0x1e are missing from the scan.

userInterface.hoverTargets: Every node and every address label shows an explanation in the Details card on hover or click.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Labeled structure diagram with concrete scan output
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Hover/click explanations plus fault scenarios that change the i2c.scan() result
keyQuestions: How many addresses does i2c.scan() print for a working 9-DOF module, and why?
How does the Pico W choose which chip answers on a shared bus?
Which robot features are lost if the LSM303DLHC stops answering?
commonMisconceptions: A 9-DOF module is one chip with one address.
Each sensor needs its own pair of I2C wires.
The accelerometer and magnetometer are separate chips on this module (they share the LSM303DLHC, which answers at two addresses).
assessmentOpportunities: Label a blank diagram with all three sensor addresses and all data units.
Exit ticket: interpret an i2c.scan() result of ['0x6b', '0x77'].
Compare the diagram with a real scan on the course hardware.
